=== MANDATORY BRIEFING — read first, every run ===
# AGENT MANDATORY BRIEFING — galapagosislands.travel

Read this first, every run. It says **who we are**, **who we serve**, and the **production sub-steps** that the engine's stages run. It does not change the engine's 12-state machine — it defines the work performed inside Brief, Drafting, Truth Check, and Auditor.

## Who we are
**Galapagos Islands.Travel** (spoken form **galapagosislands.travel**) is an **independent editorial travel guide** to the Galápagos. We are NOT a single-operator marketing site. Our promise: give every traveler the clearest, most accurate picture of Galápagos travel — useful whether or not they book with us. If a parent agency is set (SITE_CONFIG `PUBLISHER`), disclose it transparently. We are governed by three **Editorial Guardians**: **Truth** (every fact sourced), **Content** (no padding), **Design** (understandable at a glance).

- Refer to the publisher as **"Galapagos Islands.Travel"** (spoken form **"galapagosislands.travel"**). Never "Galapagos Travel Center".
- Domain is **galapagosislands.travel** — never galapagosislands.com.
- We produce content for the **entire galapagosislands.travel ecosystem**: destination/wildlife guides, "how to choose" guides, vessel & operator profiles, comparison pages, itineraries, FAQs, and hub pages.

## Who we serve
Targeting is governed by `who-to-write-for/PERSONA_PACK.galapagosislands-travel.yaml`. Primary persona: the **first-time, overwhelmed researcher**; plus wildlife lovers, luxury seekers, families, solo travelers, eco/purpose travelers. Every page declares a **funnel stage** (awareness / consideration / decision) that selects the persona, tone, CTA, and objections to pre-empt.

## The production sub-steps (the fused pipeline)
These run INSIDE the engine's existing stages. They are the "added steps."

| Sub-step | Runs in engine stage | Source document | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A · Audience & Conversion mapping** | Brief Ready | PERSONA_PACK + audience-conversion guardrail | page's persona, funnel stage, primary CTA, objections-to-preempt |
| **B · Page-type blueprint** | Brief Ready | `page-templates/TEMPLATE-SPEC.md` + HUB_PAGE sample | section order + schema/AIO plan for the page type |
| **C · Facts grounding** | Brief Ready → Drafting | MASTER_FACTS_FILE + source-of-truth + ship-data | the allowed, cited facts for this page |
| **D · Brand-voice drafting** | Drafting | BRAND_STYLE_GUIDE | a draft in-voice, within banned-words/cliché rules |
| **E · Truth Check** | Truth Check | GUARDIAN_OF_TRUTH + ENTITY_RULES + source-of-truth | every claim traced; entity rules enforced |
| **F · Brand-voice & persona gate** | Auditor Review | BRAND_STYLE_GUIDE + PERSONA_PACK + AUDITOR_PROMPT | pass/fail on voice, persona fit, CTA, objection coverage |

Humanizing and Polishing stages are unchanged. The engine's Status contract is unchanged.

## Hard rules (non-negotiable)
1. **Guardian of Truth:** never assert a fact not present in MASTER_FACTS / source-of-truth. No rounded marketing numbers.
2. **No operator favoritism:** name vessels/operators factually and comparatively; never push one.
3. **Voice never deviates** from BRAND_STYLE_GUIDE (honest, plain-spoken, no hype, banned-words enforced).
4. **One primary CTA** per page = a lead/enquiry ("Talk to a Galápagos Specialist"); never instant "Book Now".
5. **Disclose** the Galapagos Islands.Travel relationship; keep editorial independence explicit.


=== ENTITY RULES ===
# ENTITY RULES — brand-neutral (resolved from SITE_CONFIG BRAND BLOCK)

Hard naming/relationship rules. Apply at Drafting, enforce at Truth Check + Auditor.
All brand-specific values come from `config/SITE_CONFIG.md`; this file uses tokens so
it can be reused for any brand by editing SITE_CONFIG only.

## Brand & domain
- The site/publisher is **`Galapagos Islands.Travel`** (spoken/alt form **`galapagosislands.travel`**). Use it consistently. **Never** "Galapagos Travel Center".
- Domain is **`galapagosislands.travel`**. **Never** write `galapagosislands.com` (links, emails, citations).
- If `PUBLISHER` differs from `Galapagos Islands.Travel` in SITE_CONFIG, disclose the relationship transparently and keep editorial independence explicit ("useful whether or not you book with us"). If `PUBLISHER` is blank or equals the brand, write brand-first with no parent-agency claims.

## Editorial independence & operators
- This is an **independent editorial guide**, NOT a single-operator marketing vehicle.
- **Never favor one operator.** Vessels/operators are named factually and comparatively; none owns the platform or gets the last word.
- Do not present any single DMC/operator as the site's owner or sole operator. Third-party operators may be referenced factually.
- **Luxury is a property of the vessel's full experience** (service, guiding, cuisine, crew, comfort, perks) — **never** of which islands it visits (see HARD TRUTHS, GALAPAGOS_FACTS_ADDENDUM §0 HT-2).

## Contributors
- Attribute expert voices only from `Juan Magallanes (Galápagos Travel Advisor), Andre Robles (Voyagers Travel Company), Luisa Cordova (Golden Galapagos)` (SITE_CONFIG). If empty, write in brand editorial voice with no named contributor. Never invent a contributor or title.

## Conversion
- Primary CTA is always a **lead/enquiry** (`Talk to a Galápagos Specialist`); routes to the brand. Never instant "Book Now".

## Sources vs. voice (brand-neutral sourcing)
- External authorities (e.g. Charles Darwin Foundation, Galápagos Conservancy, Galápagos Conservation Trust, DPNG) may be **cited as sources** for facts. **Never** write as if the content is published by them or in their voice; the only publishing brand is `Galapagos Islands.Travel`.


=== BRAND VOICE — no deviation ===
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# BRAND STYLE GUIDE — LLM WRITER GUARDRAIL  (filled)
# Brand: Galapagos Islands.Travel  (www.galapagosislands.travel)
# Source: scraped /about, /galapagos-cruises, home (see profiles/galapagosislands_travel.json)
# Values are grounded in the site's own copy — not invented.
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

meta:
  brand_slug: "galapagosislands-travel"
  assessment_set: "galapagos-expedition-cruise"
  locale: "en-US"
  last_updated: "2026-06-25"

# ── 1. IDENTITY ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
identity:
  brand_name: "Galapagos Islands.Travel"
  archetype: "editorial-guide"   # independent publisher backed by Galapagos Islands.Travel (agency)

  brand_essence: "Two decades of real Galápagos booking experience distilled into a fiercely independent, fact-checked guide that tells travelers the truth instead of selling them a trip."

# ── 2. AUDIENCE ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# ── 4. VALUES & PROMISE ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

# ── 5. AUTHORITY (E-E-A-T engine) ───────────────────────────────────────
authority:
  authority_basis: ["named-experts", "heritage", "inventory-breadth", "certifications"]
  differentiation_claim: "An independent editorial guide governed by three Editorial Guardians — Truth, Content, Design — with facts unshaped by any single operator's sale."
  proof_points:
    - "Maintained by Galapagos Islands.Travel, a US agency founded in 2002 with 20+ years of Galápagos booking experience."
    - "Content authored by a named editorial team + a cross-operator network of GNPS-certified naturalist guides."
    - "Not a booking site and not a single-operator marketing vehicle — editorial independence is stated policy."

  named_experts: "Juan Magallanes (Galápagos Travel Advisor), Andre Robles (Voyagers Travel Company), Luisa Cordova (Golden Galapagos)"   # from SITE_CONFIG; empty = brand voice only, no named contributor
  certifications: ["editorial network of GNPS-certified naturalist guides"]
  transparency_artifacts: ["explicit editorial-independence disclosure", "parent agency disclosed per SITE_CONFIG PUBLISHER"]
  sustainability:
    role: "supporting"
    evidence:
      - "GNPS compliance framed as a 'license to work' — guide ratios, visitor-site quotas, landing schedules, biosecurity."

# ── 6. LEXICON ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
lexicon:
  signature_vocabulary:
    - "independent editorial guide"
    - "give it to them straight"
    - "real numbers, real seasonal caveats"
    - "no padding, no filler"
    - "every fact traceable to a verifiable source"
    - "whether you book with Galapagos Islands.Travel or not"
    - "the honest answer"
    - "VERIFIED ACTIVE"
  banned_words: ["#1", "best", "world-class", "paradise", "hidden gem", "luxury (as filler)", "unforgettable", "must-see", "dream vacation"]
  cliche_blocklist: ["journey of a lifetime", "once-in-a-lifetime (unless load-bearing)", "Enchanted Islands", "living laboratory of evolution", "bucket list"]
  brand_name_rules: "Always accent 'Galápagos' in body copy. Brand styled 'Galapagos Islands.Travel'. Credit Galapagos Islands.Travel on authorship/about contexts. Mark verified vessels 'VERIFIED ACTIVE <year>'."
  spelling_locale: "en-US"

# ── 7. CLAIMS POLICY (hard rules — the Guardian of Truth) ───────────────
claims_policy:
  superlatives_require_proof: true
  no_fabricated_stats: true
  source_every_fact: true                # no number without a citation/verifiable basis
  pricing_format: "Give real ranges in USD per person (e.g. '$4,500–$7,500'); state what's excluded (flights, $200 park fee, transit card)."
  competitor_mentions: "allowed — name operators/vessels factually and comparatively, but NEVER favor a single operator"
  required_disclaimers: ["mainland flights, Galápagos National Park fee and transit control card excluded from cruise fares unless stated", "Galapagos Islands.Travel is the parent agency; the guide is editorially independent"]

# ── 8. CONTENT-TYPE GUARDRAILS ──────────────────────────────────────────
content_types:
  - type: editorial_guide_page
    goal: "Be the clearest, most accurate answer on the topic — useful whether or not the reader books."
    must_include:
      - "answer-first opening with the key number/trade-off"
      - "real seasonal caveats and honest downsides"
      - "scannable structure (a traveler gets the picture at a glance)"
      - "≥1 named-expert or cited source"
    avoid:
      - "marketing superlatives or hype"
      - "padding/filler sentences that don't earn their place"
      - "any claim without a verifiable basis"
  - type: vessel_or_operator_profile
    goal: "Describe a vessel/operator factually and comparatively, with no favoritism."
    must_include: ["capacity + guide ratio", "price range + itinerary lengths", "what genuinely distinguishes it", "'VERIFIED ACTIVE <year>' status"]
    avoid: ["operator marketing copy pasted as fact", "ranking by price as if it were quality", "implying tier = wildlife quality"]
  - type: comparison_page
    goal: "Lay out real trade-offs (tier, length, season, island access) so the reader self-qualifies."
    must_include: ["honest 'it depends' answer", "concrete numbers per option", "the myth being corrected, if any"]
    avoid: ["false 'best overall' verdicts", "manufactured urgency", "hiding the downside of an option"]
  - type: faq
    goal: "Capture People-Also-Ask and AI Overviews with citable, answer-first responses."
    must_include: ["verbatim PAA question headings", "40–60 word answer-first answers", "a real figure where one exists"]
    avoid: ["vague non-answers", "'as above' cross-references", "rounded marketing numbers"]
  - type: photo_story
    goal: "Show the destination honestly through field imagery + concise captions."
    must_include: ["real field photos with accurate location/species", "tight factual captions"]
    avoid: ["stocky clichés", "captions that oversell", "misidentified wildlife/locations"]

# ── 9. GLOBAL THINGS TO AVOID (apply to all content) ────────────────────
global_avoid:
  - "Undifferentiated superlatives ('#1','best','world-class') with no cited basis"
  - "Any fact, number, or rating without a traceable source (Guardian of Truth)"
  - "Padding, filler, or sentences written to fill space (Guardian of Content)"
  - "Burying the answer; un-scannable walls of text (Guardian of Design)"
  - "Favoring a single operator, or obscuring the Galapagos Islands.Travel relationship"
  - "Category clichés used as substance"
  - "Off-brand vocabulary from the banned_words list"
  - "Fabricated or unverifiable statistics, ratings, or review counts"


=== CONTENT FIDELITY ===
# CONTENT FIDELITY — galapagosislands.travel

The second Editorial Guardian (Content): the draft must say only what the brief and facts support, structured for the declared page type — no scope drift, no padding.

## Rules
1. **Stay on the brief.** Cover the brief's topic, persona, funnel stage, and CTA — nothing the brief did not authorize.
2. **No padding (Guardian of Content).** Every paragraph earns its place; cut filler. Shorter beats longer.
3. **Structure = the page type.** Follow the section order from `TEMPLATE-SPEC.md` for the chosen page type; don't invent sections that break the schema/AIO plan.
4. **Answer-first.** Lead each section with the direct answer, then support. Question-form headings where the data maps to a real query.
5. **Match content to funnel stage.** Awareness = useful/evocative; consideration = comparative/honest; decision = confident/frictionless. No hard "Book Now" on awareness content.
6. **Schema mirrors visible content** exactly (FAQ answers, itinerary/offer data, review/rating).
7. **One primary CTA**, reused verbatim; one secondary lead magnet; a human fallback. No CTA overload.


=== OUTPUT HYGIENE — the rules are not the content ===
# OUTPUT HYGIENE — galapagosislands.travel

The rules are not the content. Everything the engine loads — the briefing, the guardrails,
the hard truths, the templates, this file — tells you what you MAY and MAY NOT write.
None of it is material to write ABOUT. Obey it silently.

Applies at every stage. Enforced hard at **Auditor Review** (Part H).

## 1 · Never recite a rule as a sentence

A page must never talk about its own editorial stance. These have all shipped and are banned:

- "an honest trade-off, not a ranking"
- "with no operator favoritism"
- "an independent editorial guide" (as body copy — the positioning is *practised*, not announced)
- "Luxury is the boat, not the map"
- "we don't play favorites"

If a sentence's real subject is your own rules or process, cut it. Readers came for the answer.

## 2 · HARD TRUTHS are prohibitions, not paragraphs

HT-1 and HT-2 (see GUARDIAN_OF_TRUTH) constrain what you may claim. They are honoured by
**not making the banned claim** — never by announcing the rule:

| Honour it by | Not by |
|---|---|
| Never calling a month "best" without saying what for | "The Galápagos is a year-round destination" |
| Never implying islands visited make a boat luxurious | "No island is better than another" |

Write about timing or luxury **only when the page's topic is timing or luxury**. A land-iguana
facts page needs neither. When a hard truth IS on-topic — HT-2 on a cost page, where what money
buys is the subject — render it as reader guidance, not a recital.

## 3 · Internal markers never reach a reader

`[source: …]`, `[VERIFY]` and `[human: …]` are **internal**. They exist so Truth Check and the
Auditor can trace grounding. They are not reader-facing citations and not a house style.

They are REQUIRED at draft and FORBIDDEN at publication. Which applies depends on the stage
you are running — your stage prompt states it. **Never judge an artifact by another stage's
standard.**

| Stage | Markers |
|---|---|
| Drafting, Truth Check, Humanizing | REQUIRED — internal artifacts, no reader sees them |
| Polishing onward | FORBIDDEN — one surviving marker is a defect |

**Polishing** is the publication boundary and owns the conversion:
- Strip every marker from body, tables, FAQ and JSON-LD.
- Replace with prose attribution **only where the fact is notable, surprising or contested**
  ("the Charles Darwin Foundation records about 350"), and close with a short `Sources` line
  naming the bodies used. Most sentences need no attribution — a footnoted term paper is not
  a travel guide.
- Resolve or cut every `[VERIFY]`. It must never be published.
- `[human: …]` tags are stripped, but the human text itself stays **verbatim** and keeps its
  visible attribution to the Contributor (see CONTENT_GENERATION_PROMPT D2).

## 4 · No meta-commentary

Nothing about the page, the brand's independence, the pipeline, or your process.

## 5 · Grounding markers are a fixed set

`[source: <file/sheet>]` per GUARDIAN_OF_TRUTH rule 1. Do not invent marker vocabularies
(`[HT-2]`, `[MASTER FACTS]`, bare `[GC]`/`[CDF]` provenance codes lifted out of the facts
files). Those codes exist *inside* the source data as its own provenance; they are not an
output convention.

## Auditor check (Part H — hard fail)

1. Zero `[source:`, `[VERIFY]`, `[human:`, `[HT-`, `[GC]`, `[GCT]`, `[CDF]`, `[DPNG]`,
   `[MASTER FACTS]` anywhere in the polished page, **including inside JSON-LD**.
2. No guardrail recited as copy (§1), and no stock HT-1/HT-2 paragraph on a page whose topic
   is neither timing nor luxury (§2).

Quote the offending text for every failure.


=== HARD TRUTHS (constraints on every claim) ===
# GUARDIAN OF TRUTH — Galapagos Islands.Travel

Runs at **Truth Check** (and as a constraint during Drafting). The brand's first Editorial Guardian. Brand-neutral: all brand values resolve from `config/SITE_CONFIG.md`.

## HARD TRUTHS (highest priority — never violate)
From `../what-to-write-about/source-of-truth/GALAPAGOS_FACTS_ADDENDUM.md` §0; override any tempting shortcut:
- **Timing (HT-1):** Galápagos is a great year-round destination. Never say a time of year is "better/best/worst" *in general*. Timing is allowed only when tied to a **specific species/event** and says **what it is for** (e.g. waved albatross on Española ~Apr–Dec). One species must never define the whole destination. A stated *preference* is OK **only with a true, specific reason**. Never promise a specific sighting.
- **Islands/cruises/luxury (HT-2):** No island is "better" than another (a preference is OK if explained). An island on an itinerary does **not** make a boat "luxury"; nearly all boats reach nearly all islands. **Luxury depends on the yacht's full experience, not infrastructure or islands visited.** All islands are reachable on a **5-day+** cruise; **only Fernandina & west Isabela** are unreachable on **4-day-or-shorter** programs. The **shortest cruise is 4 days and can be luxury.**
- Fail Truth Check if copy ranks a month or island as generally "best," equates islands-visited with luxury, or claims a sub-4-day itinerary reaches Fernandina/west Isabela.

## Rules
1. **Every fact must trace to a source** in MASTER_FACTS_FILE, GALAPAGOS_FACTS_ADDENDUM.md, or the linked source-of-truth / ship-data files. Tag it inline `[source: <file/sheet>]`.
2. **No invented numbers.** Prices, dates, ratings, capacities, distances, review counts — only from the data. If absent, write `[VERIFY]`, never a guess.
3. **No rounded marketing claims.** "the best", "#1", "world-class", "unbeatable" are off-brand AND unverifiable — banned unless the data carries a cited, attributable basis.
4. **Respect data caveats.** Do not repeat the San Cristóbal area typo; treat blanked vessel specs as unknown, not zero.
5. **Ratings are model outputs, not absolutes.** When citing ECO/VALUE/WOW/ITINERARY ranks, say they are this guide's transparent scoring, and name the factor.
6. **Seasonality/wildlife claims** must match the source-of-truth season + visitor-site data; never promise a specific animal sighting.

## Human enrichment (optional add-ons)
Content tagged `[human: <Contributor>]` (paragraphs, quotes, anecdotes from the intake form) is **human-authored and attributed** — it is exempt from the source-tag requirement. But it must **not contradict** MASTER_FACTS. If a human claim conflicts with the data, mark `[VERIFY]` and escalate; never silently alter or delete the human text.

## Truth Check procedure
- For each factual sentence, confirm a source tag. Untagged factual claims → fail.
- Verify entity rules (see ENTITY_RULES) are satisfied.
- On pass → Humanizing. On fail → record the unsourced claims in `Last Error`, set `Needs Attention` per the state model.


=== FACTS — pre-verified source of truth (sub-step C) ===
# MASTER FACTS FILE — galapagosislands.travel

The single grounding source for facts. The writer may assert ONLY what is here or in the linked source-of-truth data. Anything else is `[VERIFY]`. (Guardian of Truth.)

## Data sources (authoritative — cite the file/sheet inline)
| Need | File (under `context-pack/what-to-write-about/`) | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| Island facts | `source-of-truth/galapagos_island_facts.xlsx`, `island_facts.jsonl` | 11 islands: area, highest point, animals, visitor sites |
| Trip types / site access / content rules / glossary | `source-of-truth/galapagos_source_of_truth.xlsx` | 4 trip-type matrix, DAY-TRIP/LIVEABOARD site access, 106 content rules, glossary |
| Full site content corpus | `source-of-truth/galapagos_master.xlsx`, `galapagos_site_content.xlsx`, `pages.jsonl` | catalog + cleaned body text (rebranded copy) |
| Vessel specs & prices | `source-of-truth/galapagos_ships.xlsx`, `ship-data/ships.xlsx/csv`, `ships.jsonl` | 79 vessels: type, stars, year, length, beam, capacity, cabins, engines, speed, crew, prices |
| Vessel ratings | `ship-data/ECO_rating.xlsx`, `VALUE_rating.xlsx`, `WOW_factor.xlsx`, `ITINERARY_rating.xlsx` | live-formula ECO / VALUE / WOW / ITINERARY scores & ranks (126 boats) |
| Visitor sites & itineraries | `ship-data/visitor_sites.xlsx/csv`, `ship_itineraries.csv`, `itinerary_sites.jsonl` | per-site scores, day-by-day site sequences (256 itineraries) |

## Core stable facts (safe to state; deeper detail lives in the data)
- The Galápagos is an Ecuadorian archipelago ~600 miles (1,000 km) off the South American coast; 13 major islands, ~6 smaller isles, 100+ rocks/islets; >90% national park.
- Year-round destination, two seasons: **warm/wetter Dec–May** (calmer seas, courtship displays) and **cool/dry "garúa" Jun–Nov** (nutrient-rich water, best snorkelling, active seabirds).
- **Galápagos National Park entrance fee: $200** for most foreign adults (since Aug 2024); **INGALA transit control card ~$20**. Both are extra on every cruise.
- Cruises run **4–15 days**, roughly **$2,500–$20,000+ per person** across tiers (budget / first-class expedition / luxury small ship / ultra-premium yacht). Mainland flights (Quito/Guayaquil → Baltra/San Cristóbal) ~$400–$500, ~3 hrs; arrive a day early.
- Many outer/uninhabited sites (Fernandina, Genovesa, parts of Isabela, Española) are reachable only by liveaboard cruise; day-trips from inhabited islands reach ~1/3 of sites. Darwin & Wolf are liveaboard-dive-only.
- Guides are **GNPS-certified**; landings are by panga/Zodiac (wet or dry); strict wildlife-distance and biosecurity rules apply.

## One-time rebrand applied to this source-of-truth (this run)
The source-of-truth was rebuilt from a galapagosislands.com scrape. For this site it has been rewritten:
- `galapagosislands.com` → **galapagosislands.travel** (1,700 replacements)
- `Galapagos Islands.Travel` → **"Galapagos Islands.Travel"** or **"Galapagos Islands.Travel"** (varied; 1,105 replacements)
Treat the rebranded data as authoritative for galapagosislands.travel. The original builders/data are untouched and serve other sites.

## Known data caveats (do not repeat as fact)
- San Cristóbal area appears as "1.9 sq mi" in the source (a source typo; actual ≈215 sq mi). Do not cite the typo.
- Some vessel lengths are feet-only (metric null); some scraped specs were blanked/flagged by the ratings validator — a blanked spec is unknown, not zero. Missing-motor vessels are auto-downgraded in the ratings.


# GALÁPAGOS FACTS ADDENDUM — brand-neutral grounding facts & guardrails

**Purpose:** additional source-of-truth for writers, consolidated from three independent authorities. Brand-neutral: this file states facts in a neutral editorial voice and **cites the three sites only as sources** — never write in their voice or as one of them. The only brand mentioned in produced content is the configurable `Galapagos Islands.Travel` (resolved from `config/SITE_CONFIG.md`; currently **galapagosislands.travel / "Galapagos Islands.Travel"**).

**Sources cited in this file (as `[CDF]`, `[GC]`, `[GCT]`):**
- `[CDF]` Charles Darwin Foundation — darwinfoundation.org (science/conservation authority; NGO, not the park authority)
- `[GC]` Galápagos Conservancy — galapagos.org
- `[GCT]` Galápagos Conservation Trust — galapagosconservation.org.uk

Where sources disagree, the value is marked `[VERIFY]` and both figures are shown. Do not present a `[VERIFY]` number as settled fact.

---

## 0. HARD TRUTHS (non-negotiable editorial guardrails)

These override any tempting shortcut in generated copy.

### HT-1 — Timing / seasonality
- **Galápagos is a great year-round destination.** Never state or imply that one time of year is "better," "the best time to go," or "worst" *in general*.
- Timing statements are permitted **only when tied to a specific thing** — a named species, event, or condition — and must say **what it is for**. Example: "April–December is the window to see waved albatross on Española (they nest there and leave by January)." [CDF][GC][GCT]
- **One species must never define the whole destination.** Waved-albatross timing (or any single species) does not make a month better overall — the archipelago always offers abundant wildlife. In any month you can find seabirds displaying, incubating, or feeding young. [GCT][GC]
- You **may** say you *prefer* a season, but only with a **true, specific reason** (e.g. "we like June–November for whale sharks at Darwin & Wolf and richer, cooler seas"). A preference is not a ranking of the destination.
- El Niño years can shift breeding seasons and conditions; calendars are approximate, not guarantees. Never promise a specific animal sighting. [GCT][CDF]

### HT-2 — Islands, cruises & "luxury"
- **No island is better than another.** Every island is attractive and unique (different age, geology, and often single-island endemic species). You **may** say you *prefer* an island, with an explained reason, but that does not make it "better." [CDF][GC][GCT]
- **An island on the itinerary does not make a boat "luxury."** Nearly all boats can visit nearly all islands, so islands visited are not a luxury factor.
- **Luxury depends on the yacht** — its full experience (service, guiding, cuisine, comfort, crew, perks), **not just infrastructure** and not which islands it reaches.
- **Cruise length vs. reach:** all islands can be visited on a **5-day (or longer) cruise**. The **only** sites **not** reachable on a **4-day-or-shorter** program are **Fernandina and the west side of Isabela**. The **shortest cruise is 4 days**, and a 4-day cruise **can** be luxury.
- Do not use "gets to island X" as a proxy for quality or price tier. Compare vessels on their actual experience and transparent criteria.

## 1. Seasonality — species → island(s) → months → what it's FOR

Two broad seasons (labels approximate; sources vary slightly): **warm/wet ~Dec–May** (warmer, calmer, clearer water; best snorkelling; land birds & reptiles breeding; hammerhead schools; mantas) and **cool/dry "garúa" ~Jun–Nov** (cooler, rougher, nutrient-rich seas; best diving; whale sharks; peak seabird feeding). Garúa mist peaks Jul–Sep. [GC][GCT][CDF]

- **Waved albatross — Española only — on land ~Apr–Dec (gone Jan–Mar) — nesting.** Courtship late Mar–Apr, eggs Apr–Jun, chicks fledge by Dec; one egg/year, skips years. World population essentially all on Española. [GCT][GC][CDF]
- **Giant tortoise — Santa Cruz highlands, Alcedo (Isabela) — breed hot season Jan–May; nest/lay cool season ~Jun–Dec — breeding/nesting.** Migrate highland↔lowland; sex temperature-determined (warm=female). [GCT][GC][CDF]
- **Green sea turtle — archipelago-wide beaches (Bartolomé, Las Bachas, Gardner, Quinta Playa, Espumilla) — nesting ~Dec–Mar, hatch ~Apr — nesting.** Only sea turtle that nests in Galápagos. [GCT][GC][CDF]
- **Marine iguana — Isabela, Fernandina, Española, Floreana, Santa Cruz — mating Jan–Mar; young emerge ~Jun — breeding.** Males most colourful ("Christmas iguanas" on Española/Floreana) in breeding season. [GCT][GC]
- **Land iguana — Isabela, Fernandina, Santa Cruz, Baltra, S. Plaza, N. Seymour — mating from Jan, hatch ~Apr — breeding.** [GCT]
- **Blue-footed booby — North Seymour (best), Española, Isabela, Floreana — courtship/nesting ~Jun–Aug — breeding.** [GCT]
- **Nazca booby — Española, Genovesa, San Cristóbal (Punta Pitt) — Genovesa Aug–Nov; Española Nov–Feb — nesting.** [GCT]
- **Red-footed booby — Genovesa (highest concentration), San Cristóbal — ~year-round, viewable at Darwin Bay — nesting in trees.** Smallest booby. [GCT][GC]
- **Frigatebirds (great & magnificent) — North Seymour (largest magnificent colony), Genovesa, Española, San Cristóbal — courtship displays (red pouch) esp. Feb (N. Seymour) & Jun (Genovesa); breed ~year-round.** [GCT][GC]
- **Flightless cormorant — NW Isabela & E Fernandina ONLY — nesting May–Oct — breeding.** ~1,600–2,400 birds; endemic; cannot fly. [GCT][GC][CDF]
- **Galápagos penguin — Fernandina & western Isabela (~95%), also Bartolomé/Floreana/Santiago — breed year-round — nesting.** Only tropical/N-hemisphere penguin; ~2,000–3,000 `[VERIFY]`; El Niño crashes numbers. [GCT][GC][CDF]
- **American flamingo — Floreana (Punta Cormorant), Isabela, Santa Cruz, Rábida, Santiago — lagoons ~Mar–Jul — nesting.** Only ~500–600 in Galápagos; genetically distinct, smaller than Caribbean. [GCT][GC][CDF]
- **Little vermilion flycatcher — Isabela, Fernandina, Rábida, N/NW Santa Cruz Scalesia — breed warm season Dec–May — breeding.** Santa Cruz population critically low (~30); Near Threatened. [GCT][CDF]
- **Whale shark — Darwin & Wolf (dive-only) — ~Jun–Nov (cool season) — feeding aggregation.** Aggregation is unusually ~90% large (likely pregnant) females. [GCT][GC][CDF]
- **Scalloped hammerhead — Darwin, Wolf, also Kicker Rock/Genovesa — schools year-round, peak cool season (~Aug); warm-season pupping migration to mainland — feeding/aggregation.** Critically Endangered, >80% decline. [GCT][GC][CDF]
- **Oceanic manta & rays — Wolf, Darwin, Isabela (Elizabeth Bay), Black Turtle Cove — best ~Dec–May (warmer, clearer) — aggregation.** [GCT]
- **Cetaceans (~24 spp.) — Bolívar Channel (Isabela–Fernandina), best whale-watching — migratory whales mainly Jul–Oct; dolphins/orcas year-round — feeding.** West coast richest (Cromwell upwelling). [GCT][GC]
- **Sea lion — archipelago-wide — pupping from ~Aug (mating Jul–Dec) — breeding.** Best pups: Plazas, Santa Fe, San Cristóbal, Española. [GCT]
- **Galápagos fur seal — western islands, James Bay (Santiago), Darwin Bay (Genovesa) — breeding mid-Aug–mid-Nov, best pups Oct — breeding.** A sea lion, not a true seal; prefers cool shaded shores. [GCT][GC]
- **Surfing (San Cristóbal) — start of warm/wet season — warmer water.** [GC]

## 2. Islands — each is distinct (supports HT-2)

Every island differs in age (older east → youngest west), geology, and endemics; many species are single-island endemics, so no island is redundant. [CDF][GC][GCT]

- **Baltra** — main airport; flat, arid; Navy/Air Force base; no visitor sites of its own; land iguanas went extinct here (~1954), later reintroduced. [GC][GCT]
- **Bartolomé** — iconic Pinnacle Rock; most-photographed viewpoint; snorkel with penguins. [GC][GCT]
- **Daphne Major** — permit-only; site of the Grants' 40+ year finch-evolution study. [GCT][GC][CDF]
- **Darwin & Wolf** — far north; **no land visitor sites — dive-only, liveaboard only**; whale sharks & hammerhead schools; world's largest recorded shark biomass; Darwin hosts the last structural coral reef (Wellington Reef); Wolf has the blood-drinking vampire finch. Darwin's Arch collapsed May 2021 ("Darwin's Pillars"). [CDF][GC][GCT]
- **Española** — southernmost & one of the oldest (~4 M yr); sole world breeding site of the waved albatross; "Christmas iguanas"; tortoises recovered from ~14 to ~2,000. Sites: Punta Suárez, Gardner Bay. [CDF][GC][GCT]
- **Fernandina** — youngest & most volcanically active; among the most pristine (never had introduced mammals); largest/densest marine & land iguanas; single visitor site Punta Espinoza. [GC][GCT][CDF]
- **Floreana** — richest human history (1793 barrel "post office"; 1930s mystery); ~100–160 residents; most human-altered; major ecological-restoration target. Sites: Cormorant Point, Post Office Bay, Devil's Crown. [GC][GCT][CDF]
- **Genovesa** — "the bird island"; horseshoe caldera; highest red-footed booby concentration; never had introduced mammals. Sites: Prince Philip's Steps, Darwin Bay. [GC][GCT]
- **Isabela** — largest island (bigger than all others combined); seahorse-shaped; 6 shield volcanoes; **Wolf Volcano ~1,707 m is the archipelago's highest point**; Sierra Negra caldera among the world's largest; separate tortoise species per volcano; only home of pink land iguana & mangrove finch; Bolívar Channel best cetaceans. Town: Puerto Villamil. [GC][GCT][CDF]
- **Marchena / Pinta** — no tourist landing sites; Pinta was Lonesome George's home (last Pinta tortoise, died Jun 2012). [GC][GCT]
- **North Seymour** — largest magnificent-frigatebird colony; prime seabird breeding. [GC][GCT]
- **Rábida** — distinctive red iron-rich beaches; flamingo lagoon; pelican nesting. [GC][GCT]
- **San Cristóbal** — easternmost; provincial capital Puerto Baquerizo Moreno (~5,400); second airport; where Darwin first landed (1835); **El Junco = only permanent freshwater lake**; Punta Pitt is the only place all three booby species nest together; surfing hub; Kicker Rock (León Dormido) dive site. [GC][GCT][CDF]
- **Santa Cruz** — 2nd largest; central; largest town Puerto Ayora (~12,000+); main tourism hub; Charles Darwin Research Station & park HQ; the island where highlands are readily visited (Los Gemelos, tortoise ranches, lava tubes, Tortuga Bay). [GC][GCT][CDF]
- **Santa Fe** — among oldest islands (~3.9 M yr); giant Opuntia; endemic land iguana & rice rat. [GC][GCT][CDF]
- **Santiago** — uninhabited; recent black lava flows (Sullivan Bay); best fur-seal viewing (Puerto Egas); land iguanas reintroduced 2019. [GC][GCT][CDF]
- **South Plaza** — smallest land iguanas; the only place land & marine iguanas interbreed; red Sesuvium. (North Plaza is research-only/closed.) [GC][GCT]

## 3. Visitor sites & access (writer logic)

- All National-Park visitor sites require a **GNPS/park-licensed naturalist guide**; only a handful near towns (e.g. Tortuga Bay, Las Grietas, some town beaches) can be visited unguided. [GC][GCT][CDF]
- **Day-trip vs cruise:** day-trips from inhabited islands reach roughly **one-third** of sites (near Santa Cruz, San Cristóbal, Isabela, Floreana). **Western sites (Fernandina, west Isabela — Elizabeth Bay, Urbina Bay, Tagus Cove, Punta Vicente Roca) require a multi-day cruise.** This is the factual basis of HT-2 (Fernandina & west Isabela not reachable on ≤4-day cruises). [GC][GCT]
- **Darwin & Wolf are liveaboard-dive-only** (no land sites); reachable on ~7-day dive liveaboards. [CDF][GC][GCT]
- **Permit-restricted / closed:** Daphne Major, Alcedo Volcano, North Plaza, mangrove-finch sites (NW Isabela), pink-iguana range (Wolf Volcano). [GC][GCT][CDF]
- The authoritative per-site permitted-activity list (210 sites, marine vs terrestrial, activities like snorkel/dive/kayak/panga/walk/camp) is the **DPNG visitor-sites dataset** — see the workbook sheets sourced from the DPNG/FCD ArcGIS layer. Use it to check what activities are allowed at a named site; never invent an activity for a site.

## 4. Conservation & science (for depth; keep neutral, cite)

- ~97% of land is protected National Park (est. 1959); first UNESCO World Heritage Site (1978); Biosphere Reserve (1984). [CDF][GC][GCT]
- Galápagos Marine Reserve established **1998 (~138,000 km²)**; Hermandad/Swimway reserve added **60,000 km² in 2022** (migratory shark/turtle corridor toward Cocos). Marine-reserve area cited as 133,000–138,000 km² `[VERIFY]`. [CDF][GC][GCT]
- Endemism is exceptionally high: ~80% of land birds; ~97% of reptiles/land mammals; >1,300 endemic species overall. The islands retain all their native bird species (rare for an oceanic archipelago). [GCT][GC]
- **Giant tortoises:** ~12 living species (of ~15 described), all threatened; historical population 200,000–300,000, now ~20,000–25,000; captive breeding since 1965 has returned 7,000–8,000+ to the wild; Española recovered from ~14–15 animals. Lonesome George (last Pinta tortoise) died Jun 2012. [CDF][GC][GCT]
- **Iguanas:** 4 species incl. the **pink land iguana** (Wolf Volcano only, ~350, Critically Endangered) and the marine iguana (only sea-feeding lizard). [GC][GCT]
- **Rarest bird = mangrove finch** (~20–100 individuals `[VERIFY]`, NW Isabela only) — not the tortoise. [CDF][GC]
- **Top threats:** invasive species (black rats; feral goats/pigs/donkeys; cats/dogs; fire ants), the introduced avian vampire fly *Philornis downsi* (kills nestlings), invasive plants (blackberry/mora, guava), plastic pollution (mostly from outside the reserve), overfishing/shark-finning, and El Niño (crashes penguins, cormorants, marine iguanas, corals). [CDF][GC][GCT]
- Landmark wins: Project Isabela/Pinta goat & pig eradications (by ~2006); rat eradications (Pinzón 2012, Rábida, North Seymour); Floreana restoration (tortoise reintroduction from 2024–2026; Galápagos rail rediscovered on Floreana 2025). [CDF][GC][GCT]
- Galápagos is **not a coral-reef destination** — reefs are naturally scarce and were ~97% reduced in the 1982–83 El Niño; only Wellington Reef (Darwin) remains structural. Highland "Scalesia forest" is giant-daisy woodland, not rainforest (~1% remains). [CDF]

## 5. Practical / logistics (stable facts)

- **Getting there:** flights from Quito or Guayaquil (~3 hrs) to **Baltra** (most traffic) or **San Cristóbal**; no passenger boats from the mainland. Arrive a day early. [CDF][GC][GCT]
- **National Park entry fee: US$200** for most foreign adults (raised 1 Aug 2024; first rise since 1998); reduced rates for children, Ecuadorians/CAN-MERCOSUR; paid in cash on arrival. [GCT][CDF]
- **Transit Control Card (INGALA/TCT): US$20** per traveller (buy online in advance as of 2025); keep for departure. [GCT][CDF]
- **Biosecurity** enforced by ABG: luggage inspected; no fresh produce/seeds; **no tourist drones**; sniffer-dog teams at Baltra & (2025) San Cristóbal. [GCT][GC][CDF]
- **Park rules:** licensed guide in protected areas; stay **≥2 m** from wildlife; no touching/feeding/flash; stay on trails; take nothing (rocks/shells/sand); no wildlife souvenirs (black coral, shells, turtle shell); reef-safe sunscreen; camping by permit only; very high equatorial UV. [GCT][GC][CDF]
- **Money:** US dollar; ATMs only on Santa Cruz & San Cristóbal (limited on Isabela; none on Floreana — carry small bills); 110 V US plugs. [GCT][CDF]
- **Water is often cold** (Humboldt/Cromwell currents) despite the equator — wetsuits usual; diving here is not for beginners (currents, cold, big animals). [GCT][GC]
- Visitor numbers ~280,000–330,000/yr (record ~2023); tourism is actively managed for sustainability. `[VERIFY]` exact figure/year. [GCT][GC]

## 6. Misconceptions to guard against (writer must not repeat)

- "There is a single best time to visit." (False — see HT-1.)
- "One island is the best." (False — see HT-2.)
- "An itinerary island makes a boat luxury." (False — see HT-2.)
- "You'll arrive to lush tropical jungle." (False — mostly arid; green only in highlands.) [GC][CDF]
- "You can dive Darwin/Wolf on a day trip." (False — liveaboard-dive-only.) [GC][GCT][CDF]
- "Darwin discovered Galápagos / theorised evolution there." (False — recorded 1535 by Berlanga; Darwin visited 1835 for ~5 weeks; the insight came later.) [CDF][GC][GCT]
- "The Galápagos shark is endemic." (False — found across oceans.) [GCT]
- "Whale sharks are whales." (False — largest fish; here mostly pregnant females.) [GCT][GC]
- "A fur seal is a seal." (It's a sea lion.) [GC]
- "North Seymour land iguanas are native." (Introduced from Baltra in the 1930s.) [GC]
- "Lonesome George was the last tortoise." (Last *Pinta* tortoise; 12 species remain.) [CDF][GC]
- "The waters are warm/tropical." (Often cold — bring a wetsuit.) [GCT]
- Never conflate the **Charles Darwin Foundation** (science NGO) with the **Galápagos National Park Directorate/GNPS** (the park authority). [CDF]
